transcript: that crossed out price can make an ordinary deal feel amazing, but the surprising part is that an anchor doesn't even have to be a price. In a classic experiment, people saw a number from a wheel, compared it with the share of United Nations members that were African countries, then estimated that share. The group shown 10 gave a median estimate of 25%. The group shown 65 gave 45%. The wheel offered no useful evidence, yet estimates shifted toward it. That's anchoring. A starting number can pull your judgment. So before opening a sale page, write down what the item is worth to you, and compare real alternatives. A big discount from someone else's starting price isn't the same as a good deal.
